Q: How can I use a custom font in Mapbox GL JS? A:

Currently you can upload them directly from the CURL,

This is how I managed to make it, when I want to upload Nunito Regular that I have download from Google Fonts:

curl -X POST "https://api.mapbox.com/fonts/v1/{MY_USERNAME}/?access_token=sk.eyJ..." \
  --data-binary @Nunito-Regular.ttf

Q: When to Use useState vs Redux for State Management in React A:

When you have an frontend you can have multiple scopes, for instance a global scope and local scope. Let’s imagine you have list of todos (global scope), you want to modify a todo, you create a local scope (a form). So basically you want redux a store in global scope, and useState an temporal/immediate local scope.

Q: PowerQuery - Reformat shortened date string to full date A:

In Power Query, if you convert these strings into "real dates" they will be displayed in accordance with your Windows short-date settings.

If you need them displayed in that format in Power Query, you will need to convert them to those text strings, but they will not be dates:

let
    Source = Table.FromRecords({
        [Attribute="ODUE"],
        [Attribute="M2601"],
        [Attribute="M2602"],
        [Attribute="M2603"],
        [Attribute="M2912"]
        }, type table[Attribute=text]),
    #"Date String" = Table.TransformColumns(Source,{
        {"Attribute", (x)=>if Text.StartsWith(x,"M") then 
                        Text.Upper(
                        Date.ToText(
                            Date.FromText(Text.Middle(x,1),[Format="yyMM"]),
                            [Format="yyyy-MMM-dd"]))
                        else x, type text}
            })

in
    #"Date String"

If you want to treat them as dates, then you can convert them to real dates and use the cell formatting options in Excel to display them in your desired format. An issue will be that you will not be able to have all of the letters of the month abbreviation capitalized. That way they will remain real dates:

let
    Source = Table.FromRecords({
        [Attribute="ODUE"],
        [Attribute="M2601"],
        [Attribute="M2602"],
        [Attribute="M2603"],
        [Attribute="M2912"]
        }, type table[Attribute=text]),
    #"Real Date" = Table.TransformColumns(Source,{
        {"Attribute", (x)=>if Text.StartsWith(x,"M") then 
                            Date.FromText(Text.Middle(x,1),[Format="yyMM"])
                        else x, type date}
            })

in
    #"Real Date"
